_provenance.determinism_note: Hard rule 5. Every STATISTIC in this file is a deterministic function of the analysed artifacts: no wall-clock reading and no RNG enters any figure, and no generation timestamp is recorded. Re-running on an unchanged tree reproduces every number byte-for-byte. The single field that varies between runs is 'git_head' above, which records WHICH repository state was analysed and must change when the commit does. To diff two runs, ignore that field.

D14_model_snapshot_check.VERDICT:
The model ALIAS ('claude-sonnet-4-6') is identical across the 2026-05-18 baseline, the 2026-06-02 ablation cells and the 2026-06-08 regen. But NO dated model SNAPSHOT is recorded on any execution record -- only the alias. An alias can be repointed to a new snapshot without any record changing. So it is NOT possible to demonstrate that the SUT was the same model version across those dates.
CONSEQUENCE for D14: a fresh arm run TODAY is contemporaneous with itself and with nothing else -- it cannot retroactively match the 2026-06-02 cells either. It would give a same-day control for cells re-run the same day, which is a different and larger experiment. Against the EXISTING cells, the nearest control remains baseline_regen at a 6-day gap. This is a stated limitation, not something a purchase can remove.
D14_model_snapshot_check.RECOMMENDATION: Do NOT buy a fresh undefended arm to fix the existing comparison: it cannot. baseline_regen (6-day gap) is already the best available control and is free. A fresh arm is only worth buying as part of a fully re-run, same-day matched experiment (control + all cells), which is the expensive design D13 priced.

COMBINED.RECOMMENDATION_SPLIT: These two purchases are NOT equally worthwhile. The utility measurement buys something nothing else can supply: A8 Path 1 currently proxies 4 of 6 points, and only real measurement removes that. The fresh undefended arm buys much less than it appears to (see snapshot check) -- it cannot retroactively match the existing 2026-06-02 cells, and baseline_regen already provides a 6-day-gap control for free.
